look_here_first: Ignore ray color first. Look for very narrow rough leaves and a usually single head on a stout little-branched stem, with drooping rays around a hard prickly cone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Texas nativity is clear, but only Hays was locked as an exact target-zone county independent of transplant/landscaping/seed-mix records in B016.

best_field_traits: narrow linear-lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate rough/hairy leaves
stems stout and usually simple or weakly branched, often one head
ray florets often droop around a broad hard prickly conical disk
pappus much reduced compared with fluffy Asteraceae
morphology_keys.habit: Deep-rooted perennial, usually not a spreading rhizomatous colony.
morphology_keys.heads: Radiate head with pink-purple rays around strongly conical prickly disk.
morphology_keys.reproductive_detail: Stiff chaff/bracts among disk florets create the prickly cone.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Ratibida has an elongated columnar disk and deeply divided leaves. E. purpurea generally has much broader leaves; E. pallida overlap requires finer floral/leaf characters and range context.
